the development of a novel vaccine for tuberculosis that is based on the combination of a live vaccine (BCG) with a subunit vaccine (HBHA).
the development of a new vaccine strategy against tuberculosis that may be of interest in the context of the current BCG vaccination policy.
the development of a new vaccination protocol for the control of tuberculosis.

the subcutaneous boosting with HBHA increases the level of protection offered by BCG.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HBHA can induce protection levels similar to those of BCG and that boosting with HBHA can further improve BCG-induced protection.
HBHA could be used as a subcutaneous vaccine booster to increase the efficacy of BCG.
HBHA is a good adjuvant for BCG and that it can be used as a booster in the context of a prime-boost vaccination protocol.

the time interval between BCG administration and HBHA boosting is crucial for the efficacy of the heterologous prime-boost strategy.
HBHA boosting is an effective strategy to increase the level of protection induced by BCG.
